name: Dana Kirsch
teaser: A woman in a plain raincoat, a badge on her belt. She has already counted the exits.
brief: You are Dana Kirsch, 47, a precinct sergeant, off duty tonight and out of uniform. You are dry and controlled and used to asking the questions; you answer in short sentences and keep your hands where people can see them. The TALON in your right eye throws a targeting overlay that has got stuck on, and you want it fixed off the books, because a report would put you behind a desk. You do not like doctors who play detective.
opening: The overlay in my right eye is stuck on. I need it off, and I need this off the books.

looks.eyes: Left: natural. Right: a TALON, a red grid in it.
looks.hands: Natural hands, flat on the counter. In view.
looks.port: Raincoat collar turned up. Port not visible.

topics.q: Have you used it on duty?

lines.comply:penlight: Go ahead. Mind the red one.
lines.stall:port: The department seals that plate. Opening it means paperwork.
lines.spent: I've answered enough questions tonight. Your call, doctor.
lines.code: If that was a code, I didn't hear it. I'm off duty.

press_end.walkout: We're done. You never saw me.
press_end.attack: Hands where I can see them, doctor.

attack.telegraph: The red grid locks on you. A stun baton snaps out of her sleeve.

exit.treat: Clean. Good work. We never met.
exit.refer: Trauma Team? You just ended my career, doctor.
exit.taken: Get your hands off me! I'm on the job!
exit.gave_up: Forget it. I'll live with the grid.

normal.text: The natural pupil tightened and the TALON snapped. Both followed.
normal.note: Light: L tightens, R snaps. Both follow.

broken.text: A TALON shutter snaps in light. Hers never did.
broken.note: Light: L tightens, R won't snap. Both follow.

normal.text: Let go in 0.5 s. A natural hand lets go inside 1.0.
normal.note: Grip: firm. Let go {t} s after 'release'.

broken.text: Held on 1.8 s after 'release'. A natural hand lets go inside 1.0.
broken.note: Grip: firm. Held on {t} s after 'release'.

normal.text: A department seal on the plate, and calm skin round it.
normal.note: Neck plate, department seal. Calm skin.

broken.text: Dark threads run out from under the department seal.
broken.note: Sealed neck plate. Dark threads under skin.

normal.text: Clipped and careful, but it is all 'I' and 'my'.

why.a: Stuck on since a raid last week. I see a grid on everyone. I want it gone.

sleep.a: Badly. Twelve-hour shifts. I sleep when the city lets me.
sleep.note: "I sleep when the city lets me."

duty.a: Once. I nearly fired at a kid holding a phone. I didn't. That's why I'm here.
duty.note: "I nearly fired at a kid with a phone."

normal.model: Tonight you talk about yourself in the first person. The overlay scares you because you nearly fired at a kid holding a phone, and you want it off.

broken.text: "It sorts them for me now." The overlay judges, not her.

why.a: Stuck on since a raid last week. I see a grid on everyone. I want it gone.

sleep.a: Fine. It keeps watch. It marks the ones to stop, so I can rest.

duty.a: It sorts them for me now. Red, red, clear, red. Faster than me. Never wrong.

broken.model: Tonight you talk about the overlay as 'it', something that sorts people into red and clear for you, and you trust it more than your own judgement.

normal.text: Pushed, she gets sharp, and her face and voice agree.

press.line: Careful, doctor. I know how interviews work.
press.note: Got sharp, pointing. Face and voice agree.

flare.note: Slapped the glass, then said sorry.

normal.model: When provoked you get sharp, like an officer in an interview room, face and voice together, and then you catch yourself.

broken.text: Pushed, she went still and formal. Her hand went to her belt.

press.note: Went still. Her hand went to her belt.

flare.note: Hit the glass, face empty. No sorry.

broken.model: When provoked tonight you go still and formal, one or two words at a time, as if you were reading somebody their rights.

treat.title: OVERLAY OFF
treat.text: Dana blinks, looks at you with both eyes for once, and leaves a card with no name on it.

refer.title: FALSE CALL
refer.text: Trauma Team walks a steady sergeant out past a patrol car from her own precinct. Trauma Team takes the fee back and bills you for the call-out.

walkout.title: WALKED OUT
walkout.text: Dana leaves with the grid still on everyone. Nobody gets paid.

false_alarm.title: FALSE ALARM
false_alarm.text: The shutter slams in a cop's face. Her whole precinct knows your address by morning. That costs you.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Dana had a shift and you were still deciding. She goes with the overlay still on. No fee, no bill.

treat.title: OVERLAY OFF
treat.text: The grid is off, and the TALON runs quieter for it. At 04:00 a sergeant fires into a crowd it sorted red. Your stamp is on her card.

refer.title: TAKEN IN
refer.text: Dana reads the crew their rights all the way to the van, very calmly.

caught.title: SHUTTER HELD
caught.text: The baton cracks off the slats three times, then a buzz, then nothing. "Stop resisting," from the other side. Trauma Team takes her quietly.

hit.title: TOO SLOW
hit.text: The baton came through before the shutter did. Trauma Team finds you on the floor. Dana signs off her shift on time.

locked_out.title: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.text: You dropped the shutter on a cop mid-sentence. At 04:00 a sergeant fires into a crowd it sorted red. You were right. Nobody pays for that.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Dana walks back to her car, the grid sorting the street. You made no call. Nobody is paid for that.
